source.publisher: Newry Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: not nominated; as a retiring member 'automatically become[s a member] of the new Council' (Newry Telegraph, 3 May 1930, p. 2); present at the new council's annual meeting (Newry Reporter, 5 June 1930, p. 10)

note: Nomination-day report for the fourteen divisions of Newry No. 1 (County Down) rural district, one member each. There was no contest; Mr. Pierce P. Fegan took Carrickcrossan in place of Mr. James Gorman, who retired, and four retiring members (Messrs. J. M'Connell, P. M'Ateer, A. J. M'Clean and E. J. Convery) were not nominated but continued as members; their divisions are inferred from the 1927 return. No nomination was received; the retiring member continued in office (deemed re-elected), not a co-option. Division inferred from the 1927 return (Newry Telegraph, 12 May 1927, p. 6); the Newry Telegraph, 3 May 1930, p. 2 names the member as returned, and the Newry Reporter, 5 June 1930, p. 10 places him at the new council's first meeting. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
